liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Mountains Of The Moon** (2 reviews): Listener emphasizes the rarity of this song in 1968 as a key reason to listen; This performance was the first and only 1968 appearance of the song, which lasted briefly [4][5]
- **Turn On Your Lovelight** (2 reviews): Listener identifies this as a classic 1968 performance by Pigpen, essential for fans; Listener notes the song was phased out but appreciates Phil's performance [8][9]

## Setlist highlights

- **Mountains Of The Moon**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 14 archived performances [15]

## The recordings

- **gd1968-12-20.sbd.miller.89663.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 3 songs; 30 min; rated 4.2/5 by 10 [1]. Said about its sound: Instruments and vocals are loud but lack clarity due to significant background hiss; This specific copy sounds better than another available version on the Internet Archive [7][8]
- **gd68-12-20.sbd.tiedrich.9532.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 3 songs; 30 min; rated 4/5 by 5 [2]. Said about its sound: Recording has hiss and requires high volume; Lovelight playing was typical for the era; Listener describes the atmosphere as great and representative of the band's folk style [5][6]

## Around the show

- Listener recalls recording the show from an NPR broadcast on cassette in high school [6]
- The concert featured Spirit, Comfortable Chair, and Country Joe & The Fish alongside the Dead [10]
- Audience sat on the floor in a friendly, peace-and-love atmosphere with long hair [10]
- Listener expresses affection for Pigpen and thanks Charlie for the recording [11]
- Show actually occurred at Exposition Hall, nicknamed The Old Cow Barn, not Shrine Auditorium [13]
- The Dead felt at home there, knowing their young fan base would dance and cheer [13]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1968-12-20.sbd.miller.89663.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master -> Dat -> CD [1]
- **gd68-12-20.sbd.tiedrich.9532.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Jeff Tiedrich; source: Soundboard [2]. Also: Taped on SBD cassette, transferred to DAT and CDR, then digitized by Jeff Tiedrich; Jeff Tiedrich handled editing, normalization, and 5% pitch correction using Sound Studio for Macintosh [2]
